0.3.3.headline: Windows finally captures the other side of the call
changes: Windows: system audio (the person on the other end of a Zoom/Teams/phone call) is now captured alongside your mic via WASAPI loopback. Uses the cpal audio library the mic was already on, so no new drivers, no config — the call just records both sides.
Calls where one track didn't get uploaded (corner cases, crashes, mid-session agent swaps) no longer fail the whole pipeline — the backend skips missing tracks and transcribes whatever did arrive.
Linux: if the agent is force-killed mid-recording, the system-audio child process now dies with it instead of becoming an orphan that silently eats disk.

0.3.2.headline: session tokens stay fresh, and the summary reads like something you'd paste into an email
changes: Fixed a bug where recordings made more than an hour after signing in failed with a 401. The agent now refreshes its session token automatically when it's about to expire — the same way it already did for read-only requests. If you hit this, signing out and back in was the workaround; you shouldn't need to anymore.
Summaries and action items now refer to you by your first name in the third person, not "You." So you can copy/paste straight into an email to a customer or teammate without rewriting.
Transcript lines you spoke also get labeled with your first name instead of "You."
0.3.2.footer: Calls recorded before this update still show the old wording — the new prompt only runs on fresh recordings. Re-summarize (#19) is in the queue so we can apply the new prompt to older calls too.

0.3.1.headline: the Windows upload actually works this time, and your transcript clicks go where you meant
changes: Windows: call uploads no longer fail with a 500. The agent's WAV-fallback path was sending a content-type that didn't match the signed URL, which Spaces was rejecting silently. Fixed.
Call detail (agent): clicking a transcript line now seeks to the correct timestamp every time. Audio loads fast on long calls too — we stopped round-tripping the whole file through fetch + blob.
Summaries hold a more consistent shape across calls — past tense, third person, action items as short imperative phrases.
Auto-detect end-of-call timeout dropped from 20s to 5s; the app will prompt to end a recording much sooner when you stop talking.
App checks for updates about once an hour while running, not just on launch.
Record page says "Syncing to cloud" instead of the more technical "Syncing to backend."
Small UI: title chips are now the same size, and the record page stacks "Recording · Transcribing" when you start a new call while the previous one is still processing.

0.3.0.headline: the one where calls stop disappearing and the portal catches up
changes: Windows: recordings stop failing after "Stop". The agent now falls back to uploading WAV when ffmpeg isn't installed, so the transcription service can actually fetch the audio.
Renaming a speaker now rewrites the transcript, summary, action items, and participants in one go — no more "Speaker A" stuck in the summary after you've renamed them.

Participants moved to the top of the call view (above Summary) so you rename before you read. Speaker names in the summary and action items are tinted with each person's chip color so you can scan them at a glance.
Web portal caught up to the agent: waveform, highlights (create/edit/delete/auto-detect), speaker editing, delete-with-confirm, copy buttons, and a themed /downloads page.

Admin: self-service profile + password from Settings, invite + manage teammates from Team, /admin/vocab for org-wide spelling corrections and word boost. Calls are now scoped to you by default, with a "My calls / All team" toggle for admins.
Recording status card trimmed — no more on-screen file paths.
Post-update welcome modal now fires after sign-in so it can greet you by name.
0.3.0.footer: Known: the Linux AppImage can still crash on some distros (bundled webkit2gtk fork). Fix is in progress — use the .deb if you're on Debian/Ubuntu.

0.2.1.headline: a few fixes that make the app actually work on fresh installs
changes: Fresh installs on Windows can now sign in — the agent creates a default config pointing at the production backend when one doesn't exist yet.
Call detail waveforms render everywhere again. A backend deadlock in peaks generation was silently leaving every non-trivial recording with no waveform.
Vocab settings (spelling corrections + word boost) moved to the web portal under Admin → Vocab. Admins manage them once for the whole team.
You'll see this welcome popup right after signing in, not just on first launch.
0.2.1.footer: If you missed the v0.2.0 notes, open Settings → About or ask us — we can resurface them.

0.2.0.headline: Account controls, a real waveform, and a bug fix you'll be glad to hear about
changes: You can now edit your display name, email, and password from Settings in the web portal. Email changes go through a verification link.
Admins can edit teammates: rename, change email, change role, or trigger a password reset — all from the Team page.
Invited users now show up as "pending" in Team, so you can see who hasn't accepted yet.
Call detail now renders a real waveform, thanks to server-side peak generation. No more flat line.
The recording timer stays in sync after you close the app to tray and reopen it mid-recording.
Deleting a call shows a proper confirm dialog instead of the browser's default.
Fixed a bug where finished calls were silently losing their transcript and summary after the vault note was saved. Your future recordings will land complete.
0.2.0.footer: Heads up: older recordings in the portal may still be blank from that last bug. We can help recover from local vault notes if you need to — just reach out.
